headline: Every jar, every line, every plant. One system.
formProduct: Spreads, peanut butter and grocery jars
label: #FFFFFF
heroLede: Bega runs spreads, peanut butter and grocery lines across several plants, for brands at home and in export markets. Here's what one system could look like across all of them: cameras on every line checking each jar's label, lid and best-before code, machine health on the fillers and cappers, and safety monitoring on the floor, all reporting into one view for your managers. Scroll through one jar's journey, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: On every line, the camera checks each jar has its lid on, straight and fully seated. A loose lid means leaks in the carton and a complaint from a retailer or an export customer.
labelLede: With smooth, crunchy, light and export versions running in similar jars, the label is what keeps every jar right. The camera checks every jar carries the label set for the run, straight and intact, including export labels.
codeLede: Every jar needs a correct, readable best-before date and batch code. The system reads each printed code and compares it with the product and date set at changeover, on every line at every plant.
objectLede: Lid offcuts, label backing and loose parts can end up near a line. Cameras over the belts spot anything that should not be there before jars reach a carton, and the same cameras can watch forklift and pedestrian zones.

vocab.alert: Four crooked lids in fifteen minutes. Check the capper.
